intro: Hey there! I'm going to walk you through Talk Shops. It keeps your customers updated while their car is in your shop, by text or email, with a private page for every car. It takes about five minutes, and partway through, you can try it from your own phone. Let's jump in.
board: This is the shop's Bay, named after your shop, so here it's Ridgeline Auto Repair Bay. Under the name, you can see how many cars are in the shop, and how many updates went out today. Every car sits in a column for its stage, from checked in to ready for pickup. The colored mark on each card shows how long the car has been in the shop, and you can pick the colors and the days in Settings. An urgency tag, low, medium, or high, flags a customer who needs their car back fast.
search: Looking for one car? Type in the search box. A name, a phone number, a plate, or a repair order number all work, and the Bay filters as you type. Or tap a filter, like Awaiting approval, to see only the cars waiting on a customer. Tap any stage heading to open that column, and sort it, for example most urgent first. On a phone, the Bay becomes a simple list, and the tabs move to a bar along the bottom, with Settings, Plan, Help, and Training under More.
checkin: Let's check in a new car. Sam Ortiz just dropped off his 2014 Mazda CX-5. We enter his name, and choose how to notify him: by text, by email, or both. Sam wants both. Then his cell number and email, the vehicle, and what he's hearing: a squealing belt on cold starts. This box confirms Sam agreed to receive updates. Then we check him in.
firsttext: And that's it. Sam was just notified that we have his car, with a link to follow along. That link is his own page for this car. No app, and no password. Every notification shows up here in the message thread, marked text or email, so the whole team can see what was sent and when.
estimate: Now let's look at a car that's further along. Lena's Chevy Malibu came in with the AC blowing warm. The tech found the problem, so we'll build an estimate. As we type, Talk Shops suggests items the shop has saved, with their prices. We pick the AC recharge, for 189 dollars. Then the condenser, for 624. Anything new can be saved for next time with one checkbox.
send: When the estimate is ready, we send it for approval. Talk Shops writes the message for you, with the total and the customer's link. You can change the wording if you like. Then we send it.
tryit: Now here's the fun part. Pretend you're Lena. Enter your cell number below, and we'll send you the same notification she would get. Open the link, then approve or decline each repair, just like a customer would. If you'd rather not, tap show me on screen.
waiting: Great, it's on its way. Open it on your phone, approve or decline each repair, type your name to sign, and send your decision. I'll wait right here.
gotit: Welcome back! Your decision just came through. Back at the shop, the answer shows up right away. You can see exactly what you approved and declined, and your signature with the time.
onscreen: No problem. Here's what Lena sees when she opens the link on her phone. Her car, where it's at in the process, and the estimate. She can approve or decline each repair on its own. Let's say she approves the recharge, but holds off on the condenser for now. She types her name to sign, and sends her decision. And every customer page links to the privacy policy at the bottom.
backshop: Back at the shop, her answer shows up right away. You can see exactly what she approved, and her signature with the time.
along: From here, you move the car along as the work happens. In progress. Quality check. Each step can notify the customer, and you decide which ones go out. And when it's done, ready for pickup. The customer is notified with the total and your hours.
archive: Once a car is picked up, it moves to the Archive. Every past repair is searchable by customer, phone, vehicle, plate, or repair order number, and kept for one year. Here's Maria's visit from last month.
settings: In Settings, you keep your shop's name, phone, and hours, plus the shop email where customer replies arrive. This is also where your saved labor, parts, and fees live. You can import your whole price list from Excel or a CSV file in one step.
plan: New shops start with a free trial, with no card needed. When you're ready, choose Starter, or Pro, which adds the AI tools, results, review requests, and more staff seats. Monthly or yearly. Payment happens on Stripe's secure checkout, so Talk Shops never sees your card number.
wrap: That's Talk Shops. Customers stay in the loop, approvals are signed and saved, and your front desk gets fewer calls. For a deeper look at any feature, open the Training tab, and for quick answers, open Help. On a phone, both are under More. Feel free to keep clicking around this demo shop. It's all sample data, so you can't break anything. Thanks for taking the tour!
bay-1: This is the Bay. Your team will have this screen up all day, so it's a good place to start. Across the top are your tabs: the Bay, Check in, Archive, How-to, Settings, Plan, Help, and Training. On a phone, the four you use most sit in a bar along the bottom, and the rest are under More.
bay-2: Under your shop's name, a line shows how many cars are in the shop, and how many updates went out today. The Check in vehicle button starts a new car. Next to the search box are filters: All cars, Awaiting approval, and Ready for pickup. Tap Awaiting approval to see only the jobs that can't move until a customer says yes. Tap All cars to see everything again.
bay-3: Every car sits in a column for its stage, from checked in to ready for pickup. Tap a stage heading to see every car in that step. Then sort it, like waiting longest in this step, or most urgent first. Or filter it to required work, customer replies, high urgency, or cars that have been in the shop a while. Tap all stages to go back. On a phone, the columns become one simple list.
bay-4: Each card shows the vehicle, the customer, the repair order number, the concern, and how long it's been in its current stage. A new reply tag means the customer wrote back, and an urgency tag shows how soon they need the car. The colored mark shows total time in the shop. By default, green is under a day, amber is one to three days, and red is over three. You can change the days and the colors in Settings.
bay-5: To find a car fast, use the search box. Type any part of a name, phone number, vehicle, plate, or repair order number. Let's try Whitaker. The board filters as you type, and empty columns hide. Clear the box to see everything again. Picked up cars aren't on the board. You'll find them in the Archive.
bay-6: Tap any card to open that car. That's where the work happens, and it's what the next lessons cover.
ci-1: A customer just pulled in, so let's check in their car. Open the Check in tab. First, choose the check-in method. Enter vehicle details at the shop is the usual choice when the customer is standing at your counter.
ci-2: The other option, invite customer by link, sends the customer a link to fill in their own vehicle details and upload photos before they arrive. It works well for after-hours drop-offs.
ci-3: Next, the customer's name, and how they'd like to be notified: text message, email, or both. Choose email or both, and an email field appears. Customers who prefer email get the same updates, with the same link.
ci-4: Then the vehicle: year, make, model, and plate. And the concern, in the customer's own words. The concern shows on the customer's page, so they know you heard them. If they need the car back soon, set the urgency to low, medium, or high.
ci-5: Before you save, confirm the customer agreed to receive updates, and check the box. Talk Shops won't notify anyone without it. Then tap check in and notify customer.
ci-6: The car opens right away, and the first notification is already in the message thread, with the customer's private link. Close it, and the car is on the Bay, in the checked in column, with a green edge.
st-1: Once a car is checked in, you move it through the repair, and you decide what the customer hears along the way. Open a car from the Bay. At the top is the stage bar, one button per stage, with the current stage highlighted.
st-2: Tap move to, or any stage, and a preview pops up. Talk Shops writes the message for that stage, with the customer's name, vehicle, and link. Edit it however you like. It's your shop's voice.
st-3: The notify customer box decides whether this update goes out. Leave it checked to send. Uncheck it to change the stage quietly, for example when you're catching the board up. Then tap update stage.
st-4: Waiting on parts lets you add an expected date, and it shows on the customer's page. Ready for pickup includes the total and your hours, and you can attach the final bill.
st-5: Need to say something outside a stage change? Use the message box at the bottom of the car. Every notification and every reply stays in this thread, so anyone at the counter can pick up the conversation.
es-1: Time to build an estimate, and get it approved. Open Lena's Chevy Malibu. The estimate section has a quick add row: an item, and a price.
es-2: Start typing, and Talk Shops suggests your saved items, with their prices. Type recharge, then pick it from the list, and the price fills in for you. Then tap add.
es-3: Tap the arrow beside the box to scroll through everything you've saved. We'll add the condenser too.
es-4: When you type something new, the save new items box adds it to your list for next time. For labor by the hour, parts with quantities, or shop fees, use add labor, parts, or fees, which works out the totals for you.
es-5: When the estimate is ready, tap send estimate for approval. The customer is notified with the total and their link, and the car moves to estimate review, where the board shows how long you've been waiting.
es-6: Until you send it, a pending line can be removed. Once the customer answers, each line shows approved or declined, along with their signature and the time.
cu-1: So what does your customer actually see? Let's take a look. Every car has its own private link. Customers never create an account or download an app. Open a car, and tap Customer Page.
cu-2: At the top is where the car is right now, in plain language. Below that, the estimate, with required work listed first, and a short note on what required, recommended, and optional mean. Parts and labor that go together, like Maria's front brake job, show as one repair with one price, so she approves or declines it as a whole. Everything else is its own item, so a no on one repair doesn't hold up the rest.
cu-3: To send a decision, they type their full name to sign. You get the signed answer instantly, with the time, so there's never a question about what was approved.
cu-4: The page also shows the technician's photos and notes, a timeline of every stage, and your shop's phone number. At the bottom is a link to the privacy policy, which explains how their information is used.
cu-5: The page updates as the repair moves along, so the same link works from check-in all the way to pickup.
ph-1: Photos and technician notes go a long way toward earning a customer's trust. Open Maria's Honda Civic. Photos you add here show up on the customer's page.
ph-2: A photo of a worn brake pad explains more than a paragraph. Tap add photo. On a phone, you can take the picture right there.
ph-3: Below photos are technician notes. Type what you found, or tap speak, and talk instead of typing.
ph-4: Check also notify, if you want the customer to know there's something new to read. Tap post note, and it appears on the customer's page.
pk-1: The work is done, so let's wrap up the repair. Open Tom's Subaru Outback, which is ready for pickup. In the final bill section, create an itemized bill from the approved work, or upload the invoice PDF from your shop system. Customers can open the bill from their link.
pk-2: When the customer drives away, move the car to picked up. You can send a thank you note. The car leaves the Bay, and goes to the Archive.
pk-3: Not every car gets repaired. If a customer declines the work, or never brings the car in, use close without repair. Choose a reason, and if you like, let the customer know. The record goes to the Archive, where you can reopen it later.
pk-4: Delete this repair permanently removes the car, its photos, its messages, and the customer's link. It can't be undone, so use close without repair whenever you want to keep a record.
ar-1: Finished cars don't disappear. They go to the Archive. Open the Archive tab. Every picked up car, and every repair closed without work, lands here.
ar-2: Search by customer name, phone, email, vehicle, plate, repair order number, or the concern. Let's search Delgado. Maria has been here before, and we can see what we did last time.
ar-3: Each record shows when the car was picked up, the total, and when the record will be deleted. Talk Shops keeps archived repairs for one year, then removes them automatically.
ar-4: Tap a record to open it, read the messages, and see the photos. If a car comes back for the same problem, reopen it, and it goes right back on the Bay.
se-1: Let's get your shop set up. Open Settings. Your shop name, phone, and hours appear on the customer's page.
se-2: Shop email is where customer replies go. When a customer answers an email update, it lands in this inbox.
se-3: Below that are your saved items: labor rates, parts, and fees. These power the suggestions when you build an estimate or a bill. You can add them one at a time, right here.
se-4: Or, bring in your whole price list at once. Tap edit, import, or download list, and choose an Excel file, a CSV, a PDF, or even a photo of a printed price sheet. Talk Shops reads it, and you check every item before it's saved. Tap try a sample price list to see how it works.
pl-1: Here's how the free trial and the paid plans work. New shops start with a free trial, with no card needed. The banner above the Bay shows how many days are left, and how many texts and cars you've used.
pl-2: Open the Plan tab to compare plans. Starter is 89 dollars a month, with three staff seats, one thousand texts, unlimited email, online booking, and Spanish customer pages. Pro is 149 dollars a month, with eight staff seats, three thousand texts, and the extras: the AI how-to assistant, Smart Replies, AI damage marking, results, review requests, and the time clock. Switch to yearly, and you get two months free.
pl-3: Choose a plan, and you'll go to Stripe's secure checkout. Talk Shops never sees or stores your card number. Have a promo code? Enter it on the payment page.
pl-4: After you subscribe, manage billing opens Stripe, where you can update your card, download invoices, or cancel. And if a trial ends, your board and customer links keep working. You just choose a plan to send updates again.
ht-1: The How-to tab is your shop's repair assistant. It comes with the Pro plan, and you can try it during your free trial. Ask how to do a job, like an oil change, pulling a component, or what a trouble code means. It answers with steps, tools, parts, typical specs, and safety notes.
ht-2: The quickest way in is from a car. Open Ashley's Jeep Cherokee, and tap Open Repair Guide. The How-to tab opens with the year, make, and model already filled in.
ht-3: You can also pick any car in the bay from the list, or type in another vehicle, and add the engine for a more exact answer. Then type your question, or tap speak, and ask out loud. For common jobs, tap a shortcut. Let's tap replace battery.
ht-4: The answer starts with a short summary. Then safety notes, typical specs, the tools, parts, and fluids you'll need, and step by step instructions. Follow-up ideas sit at the bottom. Tap one, and the assistant remembers the vehicle and what it already told you. Copy puts the whole answer on your clipboard, to paste into notes or a work order.
ht-5: One important thing. These answers are AI guidance for trained technicians, not factory data. Always confirm torque specs, fluid types and capacities, and procedures in the manufacturer's service information. And leave high voltage, airbag, and AC refrigerant work to certified techs. In this demo, the answers are samples.
es-pri: Each line also gets a priority. Required means it's needed to fix the concern, or for safety. Recommended means it should be done soon, to prevent bigger problems. Optional can wait. New lines start as recommended. Let's mark the condenser as optional. The customer sees these labels on their page, with required work listed first.
tm-1: Have more than one person at the shop? Let's add your team. Open Settings, and scroll to Team. Everyone at your shop gets their own sign in, so you always know who did what.
tm-2: There are two roles. Owners manage shop settings, saved prices, the plan and billing, final bills, and the team, and they send estimates for approval. Technicians work the cars: check-ins, stages, notes, photos, estimate lines, messages, and the How-to assistant.
tm-3: Your plan sets how many seats you have. Starter has three staff seats, with up to two owners. Pro has eight, with up to three owners. A pending invite holds a seat until it's accepted or canceled.
tm-4: To add someone, type their email and name, pick a role, and tap send invite. They get an email with a link. You can also copy the link and text it to them. It works once, and expires in seven days.
tm-5: Need a change? Switch a person's role right here. Send an invite again, or cancel it. And when someone leaves, tap remove, and they lose access to your shop right away.
tm-6: Each person needs their own login, because their name goes on their notes, messages, and time clock. One login works on two devices at a time, like a phone and a shop computer. Signing in on a third device signs out the oldest one. You can see how many devices each person is on, and tap sign out all devices if a phone goes missing.
sm-1: Smart Replies is a Pro feature, and it's included in your free trial. When customers text your shop, it can answer the routine questions for you. Open a car, and scroll to Messages.
sm-2: In this demo, you can try a sample customer text. Let's send, how's my car coming? With auto-reply off, Talk Shops drafts a suggested answer, with the car's current stage.
sm-3: Now turn on auto-reply, and try, what are your hours. This time, the answer goes out right away, with your posted shop hours. Routine questions get answered, even when the front desk is busy.
sm-4: Some questions need a person. When a customer asks, is my car safe to drive? Nothing is sent automatically. The message waits for your team to review and answer.
sm-5: Choose which questions get automatic answers in Settings: repair status, posted shop hours, and resending the estimate link. Leave them all unchecked, and every reply waits for staff review. Under schedule and signature, you can auto-send only outside your shop hours, and sign replies with your team's name.
si-1: Here's how signing in works, and what to do if you forget your password. Every person at your shop signs in with their own account. Use Continue with Google, or your work email and password. New shop? Tap create an account. Joining a shop's team? Open your invite, and sign up with the email it was sent to.
si-2: Forgot your password? Tap forgot password, and enter the email you sign in with. You can get a six-digit code by email, or by text, to a phone you've verified.
si-3: Let's have it texted. Enter the code, choose a new password with at least eight characters, and tap set new password. You're signed right back in.
si-4: To get reset codes by text, add a password reset phone. Open Settings, and scroll to Password reset phone. Enter your mobile number, and tap text me a code.
si-5: Enter the code we text you, and your phone is verified. You can change it or remove it anytime. And you can always reset your password by email, right from the sign-in page. Stuck? Need help on the sign-in page opens Help and Support.
wk-1: A walk-through is a quick check of the whole car. Open a car, and find Vehicle Walk-Through. There's one at check-in, and one after the repair, and your customer sees both.
wk-2: Tap Start Check. There are eleven quick points, from body and glass to dashboard warning lights. Tap good, watch, or repair for each one you check. Here, the battery tested weak, so we'll mark it repair, and add a note the customer will read.
wk-3: Checked the rest and it's all fine? Tap mark the rest good. Add the mileage, and a short summary if you like. Leave notify checked, and the customer gets a link to the report. Then save.
wk-4: When the work is done, tap Start Check under After Repair. It begins as a copy of the check-in, so you only change what's different. The new battery is in, so battery is now good. Save it.
wk-5: On the customer's page, the walk-through shows check-in and after, side by side, with anything that needs attention at the top. Your customer can see exactly what you checked, and what changed.
wa-1: Walk-around photos give you a record of the car's condition. They're great for body work, or for showing a scratch was already there. Open a car, and find Walk-around photos. Tap ask for walk-around photos, and leave notify checked, so the customer gets the link.
wa-2: On the customer's page, Talk Shops guides them through eight shots: the front, the back, both sides, and all four corners. A little map shows exactly where to stand. They tap take photo for each one, and they can retake any shot.
wa-3: Back in the shop, here's a car where the customer already sent all eight photos. On the Pro plan, and during your free trial, tap find damage with AI.
wa-4: The AI only suggests. Tap a photo to review it. Here, it found a scratch on the rear bumper. That's real, so tap confirm. You can also change the type of damage, edit the note, or tap the photo to add a mark yourself.
wa-5: On the passenger side, it marked a scuff, but that's just a reflection. Tap remove, then save. Only the marks you confirm ever reach the customer.
wa-6: Now the customer sees their photos, with every confirmed mark, and a list of the damage noted by the shop. You both have the same record, before any work begins.
ci-7: Got a number wrong, or the customer would rather get email? Open the car, and tap Edit Customer Info. Change the name, phone, email, or how they're notified. When you change how you reach them, confirm consent again. Saving doesn't send a message.
se-5: Vehicle age colors decide when cars on the Bay change from green, to amber, to red. Set how many days until a car shows a warning, and when it's overdue, and pick your own colors. The preview shows exactly how it will look. Tap save, and it applies for everyone in your shop.
hp-1: Stuck on something? That's what Help is for. Open the Help tab. Quick guides walk through everyday tasks, like checking in a car, or updating customer info, and each one links to its lesson. Below that are answers to common questions.
hp-2: Still stuck? Fill in the contact form with what happened, and the Talk Shops team replies by email. Please leave out passwords and customer details.
wd-1: A few tools help you run your day, and they sit in the bar above the Bay. Tap My Cars, and the Bay shows only the cars assigned to you, so each technician sees their own work. Tap it again to see every car.
wd-2: Next to it, Talk Shops counts the cars that are late, or due soon. A car is late once its promised by time has passed, and its card says so, so nobody gets surprised at pickup. You set the promised time at check-in, or in the car's job details.
wd-3: Turn on Alerts, and this computer plays a chime when a customer replies or approves work. If you allow notifications, you'll get one even while you're working in another window.
wd-4: At the end of the day, tap Today's Summary. It shows how many cars came in and went out, the total for cars picked up, approvals, cars finished by each tech, and anything past its promised time. Tap Done to close it.
qc-1: A few shortcuts make check-in a lot faster. Open Check in. If the customer has been here before, start typing their name, phone, plate, or VIN in the returning customer box. Tap the match, and their contact details and car fill in for you.
qc-2: For a new customer, start typing the make and model, and Talk Shops suggests them as you type, so they're spelled the same every time. In your shop, you can also enter the VIN and tap decode to fill in the car, and the car's page links to its open safety recalls.
qc-3: For routine work, pick a quick service, like an oil change and tire rotation. Its items go straight onto the estimate. If the customer already okayed the price at the counter, check fast lane. Talk Shops skips diagnosis and approval, and the car goes right to in progress.
qc-4: Add the mileage in, a promised by time, and the technician. The tech finds the car under My Cars, and the promised time shows on its card.
qc-5: You make your own quick services in Settings, under Quick Services. Give it a name, check the saved items it includes, and choose whether it can use the fast lane. Then add it, and it's ready at check-in.
jd-1: Every car keeps its job details, past visits, and reminder texts in one place. Open a car, and find Job Details. It's shop only, so the customer never sees it. Change the technician, the promised by time, and the mileage in and out right here.
jd-2: Need it on paper? Print Work Order makes a sheet for the tech, with the car, the concern, and the work to do. Once the final bill is made, Print Bill gives the customer an itemized copy at pickup.
jd-3: Past Visits lists this customer's earlier repairs, matched by phone number, plate, or VIN, with the date, mileage, total, and any work they declined. That makes it easy to bring up what you recommended last time.
jd-4: Technician notes are shared with the customer, unless you check shop only. Use it for things like a part number, or a heads up for the next tech. The customer never sees those notes.
jd-5: Reminder texts bring customers back. When work is declined, Talk Shops writes a reminder about it. Pick when it goes out, in 30, 90, or 180 days, edit the words if you like, and schedule it. You can cancel it any time before it's sent.
jd-6: Every customer can opt out. Their page has a stop reminder texts button, and if they reply STOP to any text, Talk Shops cancels their reminders.
wk-6: For tires, enter the tread depth for each one, in 32nds of an inch. Two or less shows red, and four or less shows yellow, so the customer can see which tires need replacing soon.
ht-6: Want to watch it done? Watch It Done links open YouTube and CarCareKiosk videos for this car and job. And in your shop, answers are saved. When someone asks the same question for the same kind of car, the saved answer shows up right away, and your techs can mark whether it worked.
bk-1: Online booking and Spanish both come with every plan. Your shop gets a booking link for your website, your Google profile, or your social pages. Customers ask for a day, and their requests show up right here, at the top of your Bay.
bk-2: Tap confirm a time. Pick the appointment, check the message, and confirm. Sofia booked in Spanish, so her message is already written in Spanish. The car lands on your Bay with her details filled in. And if you're full that day, tap decline, and the customer gets a polite note instead.
bk-3: To set it up, open Settings, and find online booking. Turn it on, copy your link, and add a short note for customers if you like.
bk-4: Now, Spanish. At check-in, set the customer's language to Spanish. Their page and the automatic texts switch to Spanish, while your side of the app stays in English. You can change it later, under edit customer info.
bk-5: Here's what Sofia sees. Her whole page is in Spanish, including her appointment. And any customer can switch languages themselves, with the link at the bottom of the page.
rs-1: A few Pro tools help you run the business side: results, the time clock, reviews, and your logo. They're all included in your free trial. On the Bay, tap results.
rs-2: Here's how the shop is really doing. Cars in and out, work approved and declined, your approval rate, your average ticket, and whether cars were ready on time. Below that, you'll see each week, each technician, and the work customers decline the most. Up top, choose the last week, month, quarter, or year.
rs-3: Next, the time clock. Open a car, and tap clock in when you start on it. Tap clock out when you stop. Talk Shops compares the hours worked with the labor you sold, so you can see how each job really went. On the Bay, a small timer shows who's on the clock.
rs-4: When a car is ready, or picked up, ask for a review with one tap. The customer gets a thank-you with your review link, and their page shows a review button. Add your Google or Yelp link in Settings first.
rs-5: Also in Settings, upload your logo, and pick your color. They show on customer pages, your booking page, and printed work orders. And on every plan, export your data downloads your repairs, or your customers, as a spreadsheet file. It's your data.
es-grp: When one fix takes several parts and labor, make them one repair. Open a line's repair menu, choose new repair, and give it a name, like A C repair. Then put the other lines in the same repair. Your customer sees one item with one total, and approves or declines it as a whole. You can also type the repair's name as you add each line.
hp-3: Have a quick question? Tap Ask, in the corner of any screen, and type it in your own words, like, how do I send an estimate? Talk Shops finds the answer in its help pages, right on your device. If it's not sure, it shows a few close answers to pick from. And car repair questions go straight to How-to.
